question: What slot 38 of the interface's elements does, which the country screens call under the AI.

addresses.name: CFixedWindow::SetTakesMouse
addresses.comment: **Slot 38 of the CFixedWindow's CGuiObject subobject table** (0x1602058; also CEU3DialogGui's). Stores its argument in byte [this+0x48] and calls slot 38 with it on every node of both child lists (+0x5C, then +0x4C) - so a window hands whether to take the mouse down to everything in it. `ret 4`. **Slot 38 of the interface's elements is whether the element takes the mouse, not greying** (read 2026-11-06, FINDINGS-frontend.md C.4): a button holding nought there returns from its mouse handler without acting on the event or marking it handled, so a click passes through it, and nothing in the slot touches how it is drawn - the disabled state a button greys by is slot 47's (+0x64 = 3). What reads the window's own byte was not found. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0xAC4030-0xAC4078: `mov byte [edi+0x48],bl` then two node walks each calling [vftable+0x98] (slot 38) with the same argument, `ret 4`. flag48b.py found it as slot 38 of tables 0x1602058 and 0x15CD494 (.?AVCEU3DialogGui@@ by its locator).

addresses.name: GuiButton_SetTakesMouse
addresses.comment: **Slot 38 of the four button widget tables** (0x15FFA10 guiButtonType, 0x16077D0 the listbox track buttons, 0x1609158, 0x16094A8 3dButtonType): byte [this+0x84] = takes; `ret 4`. The byte is read by the button's mouse handler (GuiButton_HandleMouse), which returns at once where it is nought. **Slot 38 of the interface's elements is whether the element takes the mouse, not greying** (read 2026-11-06, FINDINGS-frontend.md C.4): a button holding nought there returns from its mouse handler without acting on the event or marking it handled, so a click passes through it, and nothing in the slot touches how it is drawn - the disabled state a button greys by is slot 47's (+0x64 = 3). The class is unnamed (FINDINGS-guistatic.md), so the name has none.
addresses.evidence: 0xACFFD0: `mov al,[ebp+8]; mov [ecx+0x84],al; ret 4`, slot 38 of those four tables (flag48b.py, over every table whose slots 2 and 33 are the focus getter and setter). 0xACFC2B and 0xACFD4C in the handler: `cmp byte [edi+0x84],bl; je 0xACFD9F`, the epilogue, skipping both the press logic and `mov byte [esi+0x18],1`.

addresses.name: GuiButton_HandleMouse
addresses.signature: void __fastcall GuiButton_HandleMouse(void* button@ECX, void* event@stack:4, int unused@stack:8)
addresses.comment: **The button widget's mouse handler**, slot 1 of the four button tables; `ret 8`. Read as far as its gates: a button whose state (+0x64) is 3 - disabled, slot 47's - takes the separate path at 0xACFD72; otherwise, for an event of kind 0 (event +8) on a shown button (+0x2C), **nothing at all where byte +0x84 is nought** (slot 38, GuiButton_SetTakesMouse); then event +0x10 == 3 with +0x14 == 1 (the left button down) sets state 1, 4 (up) over a held button state 2 and the press is run (0xACFEA0, 0xACFEC0, the global hook at rva 0x1685878, 0xACFF00, slot 68); 5 sets state 0; the right button's down and up at +0x70; kind 1 (a move) the same +0x84 gate. Event +0x18 = 1 marks it handled. The event's layout is inferred from these uses; the second argument is not read in what was read.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0xACFBE0-0xACFDA5. The kinds and buttons are read off the compares; that 3/4/5 are down, up and leave and +0x14 the button is inferred from the state written (1 held, 2 pressed, 0) - hence inferred.

addresses.name: GuiListbox_SetTakesMouse

So a list hands whether to take the mouse to its rows. **Slot 38 of the interface's elements is whether the element takes the mouse, not greying** (read 2026-11-06, FINDINGS-frontend.md C.4): a button holding nought there returns from its mouse handler without acting on the event or marking it handled, so a click passes through it, and nothing in the slot touches how it is drawn - the disabled state a button greys by is slot 47's (+0x64 = 3).
addresses.evidence: 0xA8BF20-0xA8BF74: the list from this-4's slot 11 walked, [ecx+0x18 vftable]+0x98 called per node, then `mov [edi+0x154],bl`.

addresses.evidence: 0xAA0870-0xAA08C1: four `mov ecx,[esi+N]; call [vftable+0x98]` with the argument pushed.

addresses.name: CCountryView::ApplyAutomation
addresses.comment: Slot 14 of CCountryView. Calls slot 38 of the main window's CGuiObject subobject with 0 when the local player's setting for this view is 1 (Ai Control) and with 1 otherwise. **Slot 38 is whether an element takes the mouse** (CFixedWindow::SetTakesMouse), handed down to everything in the window: so under the AI **the screen stops taking clicks and looks exactly as before** - nothing is greyed. It was recorded as 'likely greys' until 2026-11-06; the maintainer's observation that the original greys nothing agrees with the bytes. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Slot 38's meaning settled 2026-11-06 off its bodies (CFixedWindow::SetTakesMouse, GuiButton_SetTakesMouse and the rest) and the button's handler; the control flow here is unchanged.

addresses.name: CCountryView::UpdateAutomationLine
addresses.comment: **Slot 11 of CCountryView.** Sets the text box `automation_setting` to what GetAutomationSettingText (0x2EB910) gives for the local player's setting for this view - `[player + 0x38][this + 0x78]` - calls its own slot 14, and has `mode_arrow_left`, `mode_arrow_right` and `close_button` take the mouse again (their slot 38 with 1, GuiButton_SetTakesMouse) - so they answer clicks under the AI. Does nothing when the window has no `automation_setting`. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Slot 38's meaning settled 2026-11-06 off its bodies (CFixedWindow::SetTakesMouse, GuiButton_SetTakesMouse and the rest) and the button's handler; the control flow here is unchanged.

addresses.name: CTechnologyView::UpdateAutomationLine
addresses.comment: Slot 11 of CTechnologyView: the base's automation line with four texts instead of two. Does nothing where the window has no `automation_setting`; otherwise sets it by a switch on **the local CHuman's automate_tech_sliders (+0x30)** - 0 OPT_NORMAL "Normal", 1 OPT_AICONTROL "Ai Control", 2 TECH_AUTOMATED "Research AI", 3 LEADERSHIP_AUTOMATED "Slider AI", anything else leaving the text as it was - then slot 14 (ApplyAutomation) and `mode_arrow_left`, `mode_arrow_right` and `close_button` made to take the mouse again (slot 38 with 1). So the technology screen's selector is the same setting as the lobby's Technology row, where value 0 reads OPT_PLAYER_CONTROL "Player Control" instead. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-frontend.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Slot 38's meaning settled 2026-11-06 off its bodies (CFixedWindow::SetTakesMouse, GuiButton_SetTakesMouse and the rest) and the button's handler; the control flow here is unchanged.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyView::ApplyAutomation

addresses.name: CTechnologyView::ApplyAutomation
addresses.comment:
**Slot 14 of CTechnologyView**, overriding CCountryView::ApplyAutomation; called from its slot 11 (UpdateAutomationLine). It goes by **the local CHuman's automate_tech_sliders (+0x30)**, not by automation[2] as the base would, and stops the mouse in two parts - the main window (+0xA8, its CGuiObject subobject at +0x18) and the leadership sliders' window `country_leadership_sliders` (+0x184, which the constructor stores) - each through slot 38 (0x98), 1 taking the mouse and 0 not - **slot 38 is whether an element takes the mouse, and nothing is greyed** (CFixedWindow::SetTakesMouse):

| setting | main window | `country_leadership_sliders` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 Normal (and any other value) | on | on |
| 1 Ai Control | off, then the folder buttons, the tree, the categories and the queue on again | off |
| 2 Research AI | off, then the same on again | on |
| 3 Slider AI | on | off |

What takes the mouse again under 1 and 2, in order: every folder's button `techtree_` + key, the folders taken from index 1 of the list the screen's Update walks (the lazy singleton at rva 0x1687B78, its vector at +0x3C/+0x40, each entry's key at +8); the element `tech_tree` (lookup slot 27, 0x6C); `tech_categories` (the same lookup); and `current_research` (lookup slot 31, 0x7C, then its slot 11 for the rows) with each row's `bg_current_green`, `bg_current_orange` and `bg_current_red`. So **under Research AI or Ai Control the tree, its folders and the queue stay usable** and the rest of the screen - the detail panel among it - stops answering clicks; Slider AI stops only the sliders. Bare `ret`. The name follows the base's.
addresses.evidence: Slot 38's meaning settled 2026-11-06 off its bodies (CFixedWindow::SetTakesMouse, GuiButton_SetTakesMouse and the rest) and the button's handler; the control flow here is unchanged.
